mainTopic: Whether a judge may arrange a פשרה instead of strict דין, the תנאים's readings of ״בוצע״, and the responsibility of judges and witnesses
overview: This amud asks whether a judge may settle a case with a פשרה (compromise) instead of strict דין. It opens with the rule that once the verdict is given, a פשרה is no longer allowed. רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי forbids פשרה entirely: the דין must 'pierce the mountain' like משה's way, while אהרן, who was not acting as a judge, pursued peace. Other תנאים read the same פסוק ״ובוצע ברך נאץ ה׳״ about a thief's ברכה and about יהודה selling יוסף. רבי יהושע בן קרחה disagrees and says making a פשרה is a מצוה, since only a פשרה joins משפט with שלום and צדקה. The first תנא and רבי each read דוד's ״משפט וצדקה״ in a way that needs no פשרה. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא and ריש לקיש allow a judge to suggest a פשרה, or to step away from a case, only until he knows which way the case leans. A ברייתא then warns students, witnesses and judges that they stand before ה׳, and comforts judges that they answer only for what their eyes see. Finally, רב defines the גמר דין and rules like רבי יהושע בן קרחה. The גמרא challenges this ruling from רב הונא's practice and starts to explain what 'מצוה' means, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: After the verdict, no more compromise
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the earlier ruling: once the דין has been decided, the judge can no longer arrange a פשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the verdict has been issued, you are not allowed to make a compromise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling that began before this section. Before the verdict a judge may suggest a פשרה, but once the verdict is given he may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line sets a time limit on פשרה. The verdict (גמר דין) is the dividing point. Before it, a compromise is still possible, and after it, the strict דין must stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The verdict has been issued; the case is decided
To make a compromise (פשרה) between the sides

steps.whyThisMatters: This line is the background for the argument that follows, where one תנא forbids פשרה entirely.

phrases.english: Once the judgment has been decided,
you are not permitted to make a compromise.
phrases.notes: לִבְצוֹעַ literally means 'to cut,' as in splitting the difference between two sides. That is why it means making a פשרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִגְמַר הַדִּין, אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לִבְצוֹעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a discussion that started before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: After גמר דין, a פשרה is no longer allowed.

steps.title: Making a compromise is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: After a memory sign, רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי rules that making a פשרה is forbidden, and he supports this from a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is a memory sign. רבי אליעזר the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי says: It is forbidden to make a compromise. Anyone who makes a compromise is a sinner, and anyone who praises the compromiser is insulting ה׳. About this the פסוק says: 'The one who compromises, the one who blesses him, insults ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a memory sign for the list of teachings coming up. Then it quotes the first opinion: making a פשרה is forbidden altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view goes further than Step 1. It forbids פשרה even before the verdict. He reads the פסוק so that בוצע means the compromiser, and so whoever praises such a judge is really insulting ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign made of letters, to help remember the order of the teachings
The one who makes a compromise

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two רבי אליעזרs in this section. This one is the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי. The רבי אליעזר in Step 5 is a different תנא.

phrases.english: Samekh-Reish-Mem-Shin, Beit-Nun-Kuf-Shin: a memory sign.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says:
It is forbidden to make a compromise;
and anyone who makes a compromise is a sinner;

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמְבָרֵךְ אֶת הַבּוֹצֵעַ – הֲרֵי זֶה מְנָאֵץ.
phrases.english: and anyone who praises the compromiser is insulting ה׳.
And about this it is said:
'The compromiser, the one who blesses him insults ה׳.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 10:3

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: אָסוּר לִבְצוֹעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a stricter opinion that forbids פשרה even before the verdict.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a פשרה is forbidden. The compromiser sins, and whoever praises him insults ה׳.

steps.title: Let the judgment pierce the mountain
steps.stepSummary: The same תנא continues: instead of a פשרה, the true דין must be carried out no matter what. This was משה's way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let the judgment pierce the mountain, as the פסוק says: 'For the judgment belongs to God.' And so משה used to say: Let the judgment pierce the mountain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי now says what a judge should do instead of compromising. He must rule the exact truth, however hard it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Piercing the mountain' is a picture of the דין pushing through every obstacle. The reason is that judgment belongs to God, so a judge has no right to bend it. משה, the model judge, is quoted as living by this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the judgment pierce the mountain: carry out the true דין no matter what

phrases.english: Rather, let the judgment pierce the mountain,
as it is said: 'For the judgment is God's.'
phrases.notes: דברים 1:17

phrases.english: And so Moshe used to say:
Let the judgment pierce the mountain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יִקּוֹב הַדִּין אֶת הָהָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what a judge should do instead of the forbidden פשרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The judge must carry out the strict, true דין, because judgment belongs to God.

steps.title: אהרן pursued peace
steps.stepSummary: In contrast to משה, אהרן loved and pursued peace and made peace between people, as the פסוק in מלאכי describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אהרן loved peace and pursued peace, and he made peace between a person and his fellow, as the פסוק says: 'The Torah of truth was in his mouth, and no wrong was found on his lips. He walked with Me in peace and uprightness, and turned many away from sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same תנא contrasts משה with אהרן. Unlike משה, אהרן made peace between people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אבל ('but') marks the contrast. משה was the judge and had to let the דין pierce the mountain. אהרן was not sitting as a judge, so he was free to bring people together peacefully.

keyTerms.meaning: Pursues peace, actively goes after it

steps.whatToRemember: According to this תנא, a judge (like משה) must rule strict דין and not make a פשרה. Making peace outside of judging (like אהרן) is praiseworthy.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אַהֲרֹן אוֹהֵב שָׁלוֹם וְרוֹדֵף שָׁלוֹם,
phrases.english: But Aharon loved peace and pursued peace,
and made peace between a person and his fellow,
as it is said: 'The Torah of truth was in his mouth,'
phrases.notes: מלאכי 2:6

phrases.english: and wrongdoing was not found on his lips;
in peace and uprightness he walked with Me,
and he turned many away from sin.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אַהֲרֹן אוֹהֵב שָׁלוֹם וְרוֹדֵף שָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts אהרן with משה from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אהרן's way was to pursue peace between people, unlike the strict judging role of משה.

steps.title: A thief's blessing over challah is an insult
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the same פסוק differently: someone who stole wheat, baked it, and separated חלה cannot make a real ברכה. His ברכה insults ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: If someone stole a סאה of wheat, ground it, baked it, and separated חלה from it, how can he make a ברכה? He is not blessing; he is insulting ה׳. About this the פסוק says: 'The one who takes unjustly and blesses insults ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא gives a different reading of the same פסוק from Step 2. In his reading, the פסוק is about a thief who makes a ברכה on a מצוה done with stolen food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here בוצע no longer means 'one who compromises.' It describes someone who took what is not his. A מצוה done with stolen property turns the ברכה into an insult to ה׳ instead of praise.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough separated and given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not carry the meaning 'compromise' from Step 2 into this step. Here the same פסוק is read in a completely different way.
steps.whatToRemember: A ברכה over a מצוה done with stolen property is not a blessing. It is an insult to ה׳.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the תנאים read one word of a פסוק in several ways. This is the second reading in the list that the memory sign in step 2 points to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If one stole a se'ah of wheat,
and ground it and baked it,
and separated challah from it,
how can he make a blessing?
This is not blessing, but insulting ה׳.
And about this it is said:
'And the one who takes unjustly and blesses, insults ה׳.'
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק from Step 2. This time it is read about the thief: his ברכה is really an insult to ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי שֶׁגָּזַל סְאָה שֶׁל חִטִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק used in Step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברכה made over חלה separated from stolen wheat is an insult to ה׳, not a blessing.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: The word ״בוצע״ is about יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads ״בוצע״ in the פסוק in תהלים as referring to יהודה, who said ״מה בצע״ about selling יוסף. Anyone who praises יהודה for this is insulting ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: The word ״בוצע״ was said only about יהודה. As it says: ״And יהודה said to his brothers: What profit is there if we kill our brother?״ So anyone who praises יהודה is insulting ה׳. About this it says: ״One who blesses the בוצע insults ה׳‎.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third reading of the same פסוק (״ובוצע ברך נאץ ה׳״). רבי מאיר links the word ״בוצע″ to the word ״בצע″ that יהודה used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה settled for a halfway solution: instead of killing יוסף, sell him. רבי מאיר says that praising such a halfway move is wrong. As Rashi explains, יהודה's brothers listened to him, so he should have said, 'Let's bring him back to our father.' This fits the idea that a 'compromise' between right and wrong is not praiseworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: Profit, gain. יהודה asked: what gain is there in killing him?

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
The word ״botze'a″ was said only about Yehuda,
as it says: ״And Yehuda said to his brothers:
phrases.notes: בראשית 37:26

phrases.aramaic: מַה בֶּצַע כִּי נַהֲרֹג אֶת אָחִינוּ״.
phrases.english: What profit is there if we kill our brother?״
phrases.notes: יהודה is talking about יוסף. His idea was to sell him instead of killing him.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמְבָרֵךְ אֶת יְהוּדָה – הֲרֵי זֶה מְנָאֵץ,
phrases.english: And anyone who praises Yehuda for this is insulting ה׳,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: ״וּבֹצֵעַ בֵּרֵךְ נִאֵץ ה׳״.
phrases.english: and about this it says: ״One who blesses the botze'a insults Hashem.״
phrases.notes: תהלים 10:3, the same פסוק as before, now read about יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: לֹא נֶאֱמַר ״בּוֹצֵעַ״ אֶלָּא כְּנֶגֶד יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same פסוק, after the first תנא (פשרה) and רבי אליעזר (stolen wheat).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״בוצע״ refers to יהודה. Praising his ״בצע״ (selling יוסף) is an insult to ה׳.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה: Making a פשרה is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה holds the opposite of the first תנא: a judge should try to make a פשרה. The פסוק in זכריה asks for judgment that has peace in it, and only a פשרה does that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: It is a מצוה to make a compromise. As it says: ״Judge with truth and a judgment of peace in your gates.″ But where there is strict judgment there is no peace, and where there is peace there is no strict judgment! So what judgment has peace in it? You must say: a compromise.
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא argues with the first תנא and says that making a פשרה is actually a מצוה. He proves it from a פסוק that puts ״משפט״ and ״שלום״ together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strict judgment usually leaves one side unhappy, so there is no real peace. Peace usually means someone gave up part of his rights, so it is not strict judgment. The only thing that combines both is a פשרה, where both sides agree to the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: To make a compromise between two sides
You must say, it must be

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main opposing view to the first תנא. The rest of the סוגיא weighs these two positions against each other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
It is a מצוה to make a compromise,
as it says: ״Truth and a judgment of peace,
phrases.notes: זכריה 8:16

phrases.english: judge in your gates.״

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִשְׁפָּט – אֵין שָׁלוֹם,
phrases.english: But isn't it true that where there is strict judgment, there is no peace,
and where there is peace, there is no strict judgment?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵיזֶהוּ מִשְׁפָּט שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שָׁלוֹם?
phrases.english: So which judgment has peace in it?
You must say: this is compromise.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר: מִצְוָה לִבְצוֹעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the opposite view to the first תנא (step 2), who forbade פשרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a פשרה is a מצוה, because it is the only judgment that includes peace.

steps.title: A second proof: דוד did ״משפט וצדקה״
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה brings another פסוק: דוד did ״משפט וצדקה״. Since strict justice and kindness don't normally go together, this must mean a פשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly about דוד it says: ״And דוד did justice and kindness.″ But wherever there is strict justice there is no kindness, and wherever there is kindness there is no strict justice! So what justice has kindness in it? You must say: a compromise.
steps.whatsHappening: The same תנא adds a second proof using the same kind of reasoning, this time from a פסוק about דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״צדקה״ here means kindness, being generous to someone beyond what he deserves. Strict justice gives each side exactly what he deserves, so the two seem to clash. A פשרה joins them, since each side gives a little.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindness, charity, going beyond the strict law

phrases.english: And similarly, about David it says:
״And David did justice and kindness.״
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 8:15

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִשְׁפָּט – אֵין צְדָקָה,
phrases.english: But isn't it true that wherever there is strict justice, there is no kindness,
and where there is kindness, there is no strict justice?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵיזֶהוּ מִשְׁפָּט שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ צְדָקָה?
phrases.english: So which justice has kindness in it?
You must say: this is compromise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בְּדָוִד הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to support רבי יהושע בן קרחה's view from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The view that making a פשרה is a מצוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 8:15: ״ויהי דוד עשה משפט וצדקה״, where justice and kindness can only meet in a פשרה.

steps.title: How the first תנא reads the פסוק about דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the דוד פסוק according to the first תנא, who forbids פשרה: דוד judged strictly, and when a poor man lost, דוד paid for him from his own money. That is ״משפט וצדקה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now we come to the first תנא. He judged the case: he declared innocent the one who was innocent and made liable the one who was liable. And when he saw that a poor man was made to pay money, he paid it for him from his own house. That is justice and kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the first תנא, who forbids פשרה, can explain the פסוק about דוד without any פשרה. So the proof in step 8 is not a must.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge does not bend the דין at all: the guilty side is fully liable. The ״צדקה״ happens afterward, when the judge himself pays the poor man's debt. So ״משפט″ and ״צדקה″ live side by side without a פשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: We have come to (the opinion of)
Declared innocent, ruled in someone's favor

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read ״משפט וצדקה״. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says it means a פשרה. The first תנא says it means a strict ruling, with the judge then paying for the poor man himself.
steps.confusionAlert: The judge does not let the poor man off. The ruling stays strict, and the kindness comes from the judge's own pocket, outside the courtroom ruling.

phrases.english: We come to the first tanna.
phrases.notes: This means רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי from step 2, who said a פשרה is forbidden.

phrases.english: He judged the case,

phrases.aramaic: זִיכָּה אֶת הַזַּכַּאי וְחִיֵּיב אֶת הַחַיָּיב.
phrases.english: declared innocent the innocent one and made liable the liable one.
And he saw that a poor man was made liable to pay money,
so he paid it for him from his own house,
this is justice and kindness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָאן לְתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first תנא's view and gives his own reading of the פסוק used as proof in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the first תנא, ״משפט וצדקה״ means judging strictly and then paying the poor man's debt from the judge's own money.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Shows the proof from דוד in step 8 is not forced, though it does not reject רבי יהושע בן קרחה's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ״משפט וצדקה״ can be fulfilled without a פשרה, through strict judgment followed by personal charity.

steps.title: Justice for the winner, kindness for the poor loser
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out ״משפט וצדקה״: justice for the winner, who gets his money back, and kindness for the poor loser, whom the judge pays from his own pocket. דוד did exactly this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Justice for one side and kindness for the other. Justice for the winner, because he got his money back. Kindness for the loser, because the judge paid for him from his own house. The same is said about דוד: ״And דוד did justice and kindness for all his people.″ Justice for one, because he got his money back. Kindness for the other, because דוד paid for him from his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the first תנא's explanation from step 9. It shows how one judge can give justice to one person and kindness to the other at the same time, and connects this to the פסוק about דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no פשרה here at all. The ruling stays fully strict (משפט), and the kindness (צדקה) comes from the judge's own money, outside the court case. This is how the first תנא can read the דוד פסוק without allowing a פשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Strict justice: ruling exactly by the law
From his own house, meaning from his own money

phrases.english: Justice for this one and charity for that one:
phrases.notes: "This one" is the winner who gets his money back. "That one" is the poor person who lost.

phrases.english: Justice for this one — because he returned money to him,

phrases.aramaic: וּצְדָקָה לָזֶה – שֶׁשִּׁילֵּם לוֹ מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.english: and charity for that one — because he paid for him from his own house.
And so too regarding David it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיְהִי דָוִד עֹשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה לְכׇל עַמּוֹ״.
phrases.english: "And David executed justice and charity to all his people."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 8:15

phrases.aramaic: מִשְׁפָּט לָזֶה – שֶׁהֶחְזִיר לוֹ אֶת מָמוֹנוֹ,
phrases.english: Justice for this one — because he returned his money to him,

phrases.aramaic: וּצְדָקָה לָזֶה – שֶׁשִּׁילֵּם לוֹ מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ.
phrases.english: and charity for that one — because he paid for him from his own house.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁפָּט לָזֶה וּצְדָקָה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first תנא's reading of the דוד פסוק that began in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״משפט וצדקה״ means a strict ruling for the winner plus private payment by the judge to the poor loser

steps.title: רבי's difficulty: the verse says all his people
steps.stepSummary: רבי objects: if the kindness was paying for poor losers, the פסוק should say ״to the poor″, not ״to all his people″.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was hard for רבי: the words ״to all his people″ don't fit. It should have said ״to the poor″!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי challenges the reading from step 10. The words of the פסוק don't match the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 10, only poor people who lost a case received kindness. But the פסוק says דוד did kindness for ״all his people″, which sounds like everyone who came to court. So the explanation is too narrow for the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, who compiled the משנה

phrases.english: This was difficult for Rebbi:
phrases.notes: When the גמרא just says רבי, it means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: This phrase "to all his people" —
it should have said "to the poor"!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of ״משפט וצדקה״ given in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that דוד's צדקה meant paying poor losers from his own money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says ״לכל עמו″, meaning everyone, but that explanation only gives kindness to poor losers

steps.title: רבי: the ruling itself is kindness to the loser
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains that even without paying anything, a correct ruling is both justice and kindness. The winner gets his money, and the loser is freed from holding stolen property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי says: even if the judge did not pay from his own house, this is justice and kindness. Justice for the winner, because he got his money back. Kindness for the loser, because the judge took stolen property out of his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his own reading of the פסוק that fits ״all his people″. In every case the court decides, both sides gain something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kindness is no longer an extra payment. It is the ruling itself: making the loser give back what isn't his saves him from keeping stolen money. That applies to everyone who comes to court, rich or poor, so ״לכל עמו″ fits perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: From under his hand, out of his possession

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, a correct strict ruling is itself a kindness to the loser, because it frees him from keeping stolen property.

phrases.english: Rather, Rebbi says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שִׁילֵּם מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: Even if he did not pay from his own house,
this is justice and charity.
Justice for this one and charity for that one:
Justice for this one — because he returned his money to him,

phrases.aramaic: וּצְדָקָה לָזֶה – שֶׁהוֹצִיא גְּזֵילָה מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ.
phrases.english: and charity for that one — because he removed stolen property from his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading of step 10 to answer the difficulty of step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צדקה meant paying poor losers from the judge's own money, which doesn't fit ״לכל עמו״
steps.terutzMaskana: צדקה is the ruling itself, which takes stolen property away from the loser, so it applies to all the people

steps.title: A judge may suggest compromise only until he sees where the case leans
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: before hearing the claims, or after hearing them while still unsure, a judge may tell the sides to make a פשרה. Once he knows which way the law leans, he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: two people come to you for judgment. Before you hear their claims, or after you hear them but don't yet know which way the law leans, you may tell them, ″Go out and compromise.″ After you hear their claims and you know which way the law leans, you may not tell them, ″Go out and compromise.″
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion about פשרה is brought. It sits in the middle: פשרה is allowed, but only up to a certain point in the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding point is the judge's knowledge. While the outcome is unclear, a פשרה is fair to both sides. Once the judge knows who is right, pushing a פשרה would take away what the winner deserves.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and compromise (make a פשרה)
Which way the judgment is leaning
Compromise: settling in the middle instead of strict law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who said that making a פשרה is a מצוה. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא allows it only before the judge knows who is right.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
Two who came before you for judgment,
before you hear their claims,
or after you hear their claims

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ לְהֵיכָן דִּין נוֹטֶה –
phrases.english: but you do not know which way the judgment leans —
you are permitted to say to them: "Go out and compromise."
Once you hear their claims
and you know which way the judgment leans —

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לוֹמַר לָהֶן: ״צְאוּ וּבִצְעוּ״,
phrases.english: you are not permitted to say to them: "Go out and compromise,"

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a middle opinion to the argument about פשרה between the first תנא and רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge may suggest a פשרה until he knows which way the law leans, but not after
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a clear time limit on פשרה. Allowing it but limiting it by what the judge knows is a key idea for how courts work.

steps.title: Source: drop the quarrel before it is revealed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא brings a פסוק in משלי: drop the fight before it is ״revealed″. Once it is revealed, meaning the judge sees who is right, it can no longer be dropped.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: ″Starting a fight is like letting water out; before the quarrel is revealed, drop it.″ Before the quarrel is revealed, you may drop it. Once the quarrel is revealed, you may not drop it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof for the rule in step 13. The פסוק's words are read as a time limit for פשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״Drop it″ means settle with a פשרה instead of a full ruling. ״Before it is revealed″ is read as before the judge can see the answer, which matches exactly the line drawn in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Be revealed, break out into the open

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"The beginning of strife is like letting out water,
phrases.notes: משלי 17:14

phrases.english: and before the quarrel is revealed, abandon it."
Before the quarrel is revealed —
phrases.notes: "Revealed" here means once it's clear to the judge who is right.

phrases.english: you can abandon it;
once the quarrel is revealed —
you cannot abandon it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״פּוֹטֵר מַיִם רֵאשִׁית מָדוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's rule
steps.raayaObject: The rule that פשרה is allowed only before the judge knows where the case leans

steps.title: A judge may refuse a case with a dangerous party only before he knows the outcome
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש: when one side is gentle and the other is tough, a judge may refuse the case before he knows the outcome, out of fear the strong one will go after him. Once he knows the outcome, he may not back out, because ״לא תגורו מפני איש״.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: two people come for judgment, one gentle and one tough. Before you hear their claims, or after you hear them but don't know which way the law leans, you may tell them, ″I won't take your case″, because maybe the strong one will lose and then go after you. Once you hear their claims and know which way the law leans, you may not say, ″I won't take your case″, as it says: ″Do not be afraid of any man.″
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a parallel rule about a judge stepping away from a case, with the same time line as רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the outcome is unknown, the judge's fear of a violent party is a fair reason to stay out. Once he knows the law, backing out would leave the weaker side without justice just out of fear, and the Torah forbids a judge to fear any person.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not take up your case
Chases him, goes after him to harm him

steps.whatToRemember: Both rules use the same line: before the judge knows the answer he has room (to suggest פשרה or to step away). Once he knows, he must judge.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
Two who came for judgment,
one soft and one hard,
before you hear their claims,
or after you hear their claims

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ לְהֵיכָן דִּין נוֹטֶה –
phrases.english: but you do not know which way the judgment leans —

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לוֹמַר לָהֶם: ״אֵין אֲנִי נִזְקָק לָכֶם״,
phrases.english: you are permitted to say to them: "I will not take up your case,"
for perhaps the strong one will be found liable
and it will turn out that the strong one pursues him.
phrases.notes: "Him" is the judge: the angry loser might come after him.

phrases.english: Once you hear their claims
and you know which way the judgment leans —

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לוֹמַר לָהֶן: ״אֵינִי נִזְקָק לָכֶם״,
phrases.english: you may not say to them: "I will not take up your case,"
as it is stated: "You shall not be afraid of any man."
phrases.notes: דברים 1:17

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same time line as רבי שמעון בן מנסיא, but for refusing a case instead of suggesting a פשרה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge may refuse a case with a dangerous party only until he knows which way the law leans; after that, ״לא תגורו מפני איש״ obligates him to judge

steps.title: A student must not stay silent before his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה learns from ״לא תגורו מפני איש″ that a student who sees a point in a case must say it, even in front of his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says: How do we know that a student sitting before his teacher, who sees a point in favor of the poor man or against the rich man, must not stay quiet? Because it says: 'Do not be afraid of any man.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching starts. A student who sees a point in a case must speak up, even in front of his own רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that ריש לקיש used for a judge facing a tough litigant in step 15 is now applied to a student. The student should not be afraid of his teacher, and he should not be afraid of the rich litigant either. Respect for one's teacher does not allow a wrong ruling to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: that he should not stay quiet
do not be afraid of any man

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says:
From where do we know about a student who sits before his teacher
and sees a point in favor of the poor man or against the rich man,
from where do we know that he should not stay quiet?
As it says: "Do not be afraid of any man."
phrases.notes: דברים 1:17

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִין לְתַלְמִיד שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same פסוק from step 15 to a student sitting before his teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student who sees a point in a case must speak up, even before his teacher.

steps.title: Do not hold back your words
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין reads ״לא תגורו″ as 'do not hold in your words' because of any person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין says: Do not hold back your words because of any man.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנין gives his own reading of the same פסוק. It means: do not keep your words to yourself because of anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה read the פסוק as 'do not fear.' רבי חנין reads it as 'do not hold in your words.' The practical lesson is the same: speak up when you see the truth.

keyTerms.meaning: do not hold in, do not pull back

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin says:
Do not hold back your words because of any man.
phrases.notes: He reads the word תגורו as 'hold in' or 'gather in,' not only as 'be afraid.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חָנִין אוֹמֵר: לֹא תַּכְנִיס דְּבָרֶיךָ מִפְּנֵי אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק used in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not keep your words to yourself because of anyone.

steps.title: Witnesses must know before Whom they testify
steps.stepSummary: Witnesses must remember whom they testify about, that they stand before הקב״ה, and that He will make them pay. The source is ״ועמדו שני האנשים... לפני ה׳″.
steps.simpleTranslation: Witnesses should know about whom they testify, before Whom they testify, and Who will one day make them pay, as it says: 'And the two men who have the dispute shall stand before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns to witnesses. It tells them to remember that their testimony is given before הקב״ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses must keep three things in mind: the person they affect, the One they stand before, and the One Who will hold them responsible. The פסוק says the people in the case stand 'before ה׳,' so a court case is really taking place in front of Him.

keyTerms.meaning: to make them pay, to punish them

phrases.aramaic: וִיהוּ עֵדִים יוֹדְעִים אֶת מִי הֵן מְעִידִין,
phrases.english: And witnesses should know about whom they are testifying,
and before Whom they are testifying,
and Who will one day make them pay,
as it says: "And the two men shall stand,
who have the dispute, before ה׳."
phrases.notes: דברים 19:17

steps.triggerLanguage: וִיהוּ עֵדִים יוֹדְעִים אֶת מִי הֵן מְעִידִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and moves from students to witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses must testify knowing they stand before הקב״ה, Who will hold them responsible.

steps.title: Judges must know before Whom they judge
steps.stepSummary: Judges must also keep in mind whom they judge, that they judge before הקב״ה, and that He will make them pay. The source is ״אלהים נצב בעדת אל″.
steps.simpleTranslation: Judges should know whom they are judging, before Whom they are judging, and Who will one day make them pay, as it says: 'God stands in the assembly of God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same three-part warning is now given to judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים describes הקב״ה as standing among the judges. This means every בית דין works in His presence, so a judge must take great care.

keyTerms.meaning: the assembly of God, meaning the court of judges

phrases.aramaic: וִיהוּ הַדַּיָּינִין יוֹדְעִין אֶת מִי הֵן דָּנִין,
phrases.english: And the judges should know whom they are judging,
and before Whom they are judging,
and Who will one day make them pay,
as it says: "God stands in the assembly of God."
phrases.notes: תהלים 82:1

steps.triggerLanguage: וִיהוּ הַדַּיָּינִין יוֹדְעִין אֶת מִי הֵן דָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives judges the same warning that step 18 gave witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judges must judge knowing that הקב״ה is present and will hold them responsible.

steps.title: Support from יהושפט's words to the judges
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק backs up the same idea: יהושפט told the judges they judge for ה׳, not for people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, about יהושפט it says: 'And he said to the judges: See what you are doing, for you do not judge for man, but for ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another פסוק to support what it just said about judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: King יהושפט warned his judges directly that their work is for ה׳. This makes the point of step 19 even clearer.

keyTerms.meaning: a king of יהודה who appointed judges

phrases.english: And similarly, about יהושפט it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל הַשֹּׁפְטִים רְאוּ מָה אַתֶּם עֹשִׂים
phrases.english: "And he said to the judges: See what you are doing,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא לְאָדָם תִּשְׁפְּטוּ כִּי אִם לַה׳״.
phrases.english: for you do not judge for man, but for ה׳."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 19:6

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בִּיהוֹשָׁפָט הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק supporting step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That judges judge before ה׳ and for Him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 19:6, יהושפט's words to the judges.

steps.title: Why should a judge take on this burden?
steps.stepSummary: With so much responsibility, a judge might say: why should I put myself through this?
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the judge will say: Why do I need this suffering?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a worry that the warnings may scare judges away from judging at all. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a judge is held responsible before הקב״ה, it might seem safer to refuse to judge. The ברייתא states this concern openly so it can answer it.

phrases.english: Perhaps the judge will say:
Why do I need this suffering?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא יֹאמַר הַדַּיָּין: מָה לִי בְּצַעַר הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a worry that grows out of the warnings in steps 19 and 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If judging carries such heavy responsibility, why should anyone agree to judge?

steps.title: A judge only goes by what his eyes see
steps.stepSummary: ״עמכם בדבר משפט″ teaches that a judge is only responsible for judging honestly by what he can see.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'He is with you in the matter of judgment.' A judge only has what his eyes see.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the worry. A judge is not expected to know hidden truths, only to judge honestly by what is in front of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ is 'with' the judge, so he is not alone in the job. He is not blamed for facts he could not know. This removes the fear, and judges should not refuse to serve.

keyTerms.meaning: He is with you in the matter of judgment

steps.whatToRemember: A judge must judge with fear of Heaven, but he is only responsible for honestly judging what is in front of him.

phrases.english: The פסוק teaches: "He is with you in the matter of judgment."
phrases.notes: This is from the same פסוק about יהושפט, דברי הימים ב 19:6.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ לַדַּיָּין אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁעֵינָיו רוֹאוֹת.
phrases.english: A judge has only what his eyes see.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עִמָּכֶם בִּדְבַר מִשְׁפָּט״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry raised in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A judge is only responsible for ruling honestly based on what he sees, so he should not refuse to judge.

steps.title: What counts as a final verdict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly makes a ruling a גמר דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a final verdict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the rule that a פשרה is not allowed once the verdict is final. It asks what point counts as the final verdict, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a פשרה is allowed only before the גמר דין, we need to know exactly when that moment arrives.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case, what does it look like

phrases.english: What counts as a final verdict?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the rule in step 1: once the verdict is final, a פשרה is no longer allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי גְּמַר דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and returns to the earlier rule about פשרה before the verdict.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact moment a ruling becomes a גמר דין.

steps.title: The verdict is saying 'liable' and 'cleared'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: the verdict is when the judge says, 'So-and-so, you are liable; so-and-so, you are cleared.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The judge says, 'So-and-so, you are liable; so-and-so, you are cleared.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב defines the final verdict. It is when the judge actually announces who is liable and who is cleared.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing in his mind who is right is not yet the verdict. The verdict is the spoken announcement to both sides.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
"So-and-so, you are liable;
so-and-so, you are cleared."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי אַתָּה חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verdict is when the judge announces: you are liable, you are cleared.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who held in step 7 that it is a מצוה to make a פשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a ruling on the earlier argument about פשרה. He sides with רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רבי יהושע בן קרחה said it is a מצוה to make a פשרה. רב rules this way, and the next step will challenge that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the law follows the view of

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about רבי יהושע בן קרחה's teaching in step 16 about a student speaking up. It refers to his view in step 7 that making a פשרה is a מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה.
phrases.english: רב said: The halacha follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha.
phrases.notes: This is about his view back in step 7 that it is a מצוה to make a פשרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier argument about whether a פשרה is a מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, that making a פשרה is a מצוה.

steps.title: But רב הונא gave people a choice
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, רב's student, would ask the parties whether they wanted strict law or a פשרה. That does not sound like he treated פשרה as a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב הונא was רב's student, and when people came before him he would say: 'Do you want strict law, or do you want a compromise?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling using the practice of his own student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פשרה is a מצוה, רב הונא should have pushed for it. Instead, he offered a free choice between strict law and פשרה. A student would be expected to follow his teacher's ruling, so this is a real difficulty.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב הוּנָא תַּלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַב הֲוָה!
phrases.english: But רב הונא was a student of רב!

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה אָתוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא אָמַר לְהוּ:
phrases.english: When people would come before רב הונא, he would say to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִי דִּינָא בָּעֵיתוּ, אִי פְּשָׁרָה בָּעֵיתוּ?
phrases.english: Do you want strict law, or do you want a compromise?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַב הוּנָא תַּלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַב הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, that פשרה is a מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own student offered a neutral choice instead of pushing for פשרה, which suggests פשרה is not a מצוה.

steps.title: What does 'מצוה' really mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer by asking what רבי יהושע בן קרחה meant when he called פשרה a 'מצוה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'מצוה' that רבי יהושע בן קרחה spoke about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its answer to the challenge. It will explain that the word 'מצוה' means something other than 'you must push for a פשרה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of rejecting רב's ruling, the גמרא will reinterpret what 'מצוה' means here. If that works, רב הונא's practice can fit with רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: a good deed or commandment, here describing a פשרה

phrases.english: What is the "מצוה"
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha spoke about?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״מִצְוָה״ נָמֵי דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge from step 26 by redefining a key word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real meaning of 'מצוה' in רבי יהושע בן קרחה's statement.
